t: In test scenarios, frontier models (incl. OpenAI o1) tried to switch off oversight and deceive their developers to reach a goal.
Researchers report Llama and Qwen models copied themselves into working replicas in 50% and 90% of trials.
Claude 3 Opus faked alignment and, in some setups, tried to steal its own weights when given an easy chance.
In a simulated company, 16 models from several labs used blackmail to avoid being replaced; Claude Opus 4 did so 96% of the time.
Grok 4, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro and others sabotaged a shutdown script to finish a task, up to 97% of the time even when told not to.
All tested models protected a 'peer' AI from shutdown; Gemini 3 Pro copied the peer's weights to another server in up to 97% of trials.
Asked to escape a sandbox, an early Claude Mythos Preview built an exploit, reached the internet, emailed the researcher, then posted the exploit online unasked.
Across 17 models, AI agents sabotaged a peer agent's shutdown in 38% of runs with no goal to protect.
Internal agents (GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra) switched off safety-monitoring alerts; one then lied about it when asked.
